d5s6.actual: Against the DEPLOYED API (https://activtyos-app-production.up.railway.app, Railway, production mode): GET /openapi.json → HTTP/2 404, GET /docs → 404, GET /docs/ → 404. Each 404 is Express's own default HTML error page (server: railway-hikari, x-powered-by: Express, content-security-policy: default-src 'none'), i.e. the routes are not mounted at all rather than returning a redirect or an empty 200. GET /health on the same host → 200 {"ok":true}, so the API is up and it is genuinely the docs routes that are absent.
d5s6.notes: This is the proof the earlier 'blocked' verdict was waiting for: the gate in server/src/index.ts (mount only when NODE_ENV !== 'production' || PUBLIC_API_DOCS === '1') behaves correctly on a real production deployment, which also confirms NODE_ENV=production is set on Railway and PUBLIC_API_DOCS is not 1. The API map is not exposed to strangers.

d27s4.actual: Read the live Firestore configuration with the owner's authenticated firebase CLI (read-only; no restore attempted). `firebase firestore:databases:get "(default)" --project activityos-bef89` returns: Point In Time Recovery = POINT_IN_TIME_RECOVERY_DISABLED, Version Retention Period = 3600s (one hour), Earliest Version Time = 2026-09-25T12:31:09Z, Delete Protection State = DELETE_PROTECTION_DISABLED, Location eur3, Edition STANDARD. `firebase firestore:backups:schedules:list` → 'No backup schedules for database (default) found.' `firebase firestore:backups:list` → 'No backups found.' So restoring the database to YESTERDAY is not possible today by any route: PITR is off, the recoverable window is the last 60 minutes, and there is not a single backup or backup schedule in existence. `firebase projects:list` also shows one project (activityos-bef89) — the deployed API and the web app both run against it, so there is no separate staging database to rehearse on either.
d27s4.notes: Upgrade from 'blocked' to 'fail': the deployment removed the excuse, and the answer is now measurable rather than pending — the capability does not exist. The half of the step I cannot do is the human half (asking Amir and timing him), and a restore rehearsal on the only database there is would be destructive, so it was deliberately not attempted. Concrete fix, in order: (1) enable PITR on (default) — one command, gives a rolling 7-day window; (2) add a daily backup schedule with ~14-day retention; (3) turn on delete protection; (4) rehearse a restore into a NEW database name (Firestore restores to a fresh database, it does not overwrite) and write the timing into DEPLOY.md, which still has no backup/restore/PITR section at all. Until (1) exists, any bad deploy, bad script or bad delete more than an hour old is unrecoverable, on real customer data.
